How the tests were run

Backend testscd backend && npm test: Jest + Supertest, each suite on its own in-memory MongoDB (mongodb-memory-server); the invoice suite uses an in-memory replica set because invoices need transactions
Browser checksAutomated with Puppeteer driving Microsoft Edge (headless) against the production build of the frontend and the real backend on an in-memory MongoDB replica set, on separate ports. Any request to the normal dev ports is blocked, so no real database is touched.

Step 6 — Weekly timesheet

Hours per project per day, Monday to Sunday, counted in the user's own time zone (daylight saving days are 23 or 25 hours long). An entry that crosses midnight is split between the days it touches. Also covered by this step: the entries list's overlap filter (in entries.test.js), used so a timesheet cell lists the entry behind it.

Screenshots

Step 7 — Invoices

An invoice bills one client's unbilled, billable time for a date range, and those entries become billed. Key rule: an entry can never be on two invoices, even when two requests arrive at the same moment. The server first claims the entries with one update that only matches entries that are not billed yet (so a second request cannot match them), inside a database transaction together with the invoice number and the invoice itself. Checked by backend tests (two identical requests, eight at once, overlapping periods, two users) and in the browser (two tabs pressing Create at the same moment, six simultaneous API calls). Invoices keep a copy of the client, the rates and the lines, so later changes never alter them.

Mutation check (do the tests really catch the bug?): with the "not billed yet" condition temporarily removed from the claim, 5 of the 32 invoice tests fail, including all three concurrency tests; with the condition back, all 32 pass. Details: results/mutation-check-double-billing.txt.

Printing: sample-pdfs/invoice-INV-0001.pdf (one A4 page) and sample-pdfs/invoice-long-36-projects.pdf (36 projects, three pages) were produced by the browser's own PDF engine from the invoice page.
